new: A **System** section for admins (Health, Problem files, Logs, Audit, Backup) at `/system/<page>`; see docs/operations.md.

**Health**: status cards (OK, warning, fail) with a fix hint for the database, disk space, Plex, Sonarr, Radarr and Bazarr, workers, queue, tools and recent errors, also as JSON (`GET /api/ops/health`).
**Problem files**: files that keep failing or can't be read, with Retry and Ignore; the item page warns about them.

**Direct-play advisor** on the item page (all four layouts): whether Plex Web, Apple TV, Roku, Android TV, smart TVs and the desktop app would direct play, direct stream or transcode the file, and why, from the index alone.

**Backups**: back up now, scheduled (daily or weekly, keep the newest N), download, delete, and restore from a file with a preview and a confirmation; the file is validated first and the current database is kept as a backup. Secrets are left out unless you ask, and marked when included.
**Audit log** of sign-ins, account and role changes, settings changes, applies, restores, backups and trash deletions, with filters.

**Logs** viewer: the app now writes a rotating log file; live tail, level, text and file filters, download and clear. Tokens, API keys, passwords, cookies and Authorization headers are redacted in what you see and download.
**Metrics**: `/metrics` (Prometheus) and `/metrics.json` (Home Assistant), off by default, protected by a token or a private-network check.
Settings, System tab: backups, metrics and the log file.

Every rewritten file is verified before it replaces the original: its streams, languages, flags and codecs are compared with the plan, its duration with the source's, a few seconds are decoded (start, middle and end with Full) and every subtitle track is read. A file that fails keeps the original untouched and the item fails with the reason. On by default (Settings, Safety and housekeeping: Full, Quick or Off, which asks for a confirmation); workers check their rewrites the same way.

Worker limits (Settings, Workers, and per worker with its Limits button): no new job while a worker's GPU is too hot (83 °C by default, until it is 10 °C cooler) or draws too much power, and none in its quiet hours (e.g. Mon-Fri 22:00-07:00). A running file always finishes, unless the GPU reaches the hard limit (92 °C): then it is handed back untouched and queued again. GPU readings are read-only (nvidia-smi, or the driver's NVML inside the Flatpak). The Workers dialog and the Overview show why a worker waits, and the Workers dialog shows each GPU's temperature.

Workers can update themselves (opt-in per worker): a systemd user timer on the worker machine (`setup-worker.sh --self-update-timer`) installs a newer release from the public feed when it works with the main app, inside the worker's update hours, and only while the worker is idle. The worker's Flatpak gets no host permission. Updates start once worker bundles are published in the feed (not yet in this release). See docs/workers.md.
changed: The database gets two new tables, `audit_log` and `problem_ignores`, created automatically at start-up. Back up before upgrading, as always.

new: The web UI can be translated (phase 1): each user picks a language in Settings, Account; English is complete and other languages can be added as JSON files (see docs/ui.md). Server-side texts and the command line stay English for now.

Themes: System, Light or Dark per user, plus custom themes (presets Plex orange, High contrast and OLED black, live preview with contrast checks, import/export as JSON), with no flash of the wrong theme; light and dark colours now meet WCAG AA contrast.
fixed: Subtitles held for your burned-in review no longer count as a failed search: once you decide, the next run adds them instead of waiting a day.
Text that was hard to read in the light theme (accent text, warnings, the Commit button) now has enough contrast.
The Settings tabs wrap onto a second line instead of being cut off, and Settings panels fit narrow phones, in any language.
changed: The code is reorganised into smaller modules, with no change in behaviour.

Every pull request and develop build now runs the full test suite with the real media tools, plus browser tests of every page in light and dark at desktop and phone size; a failing run blocks the Docker image.
Browsers check for updated scripts and styles on every load, so an upgrade never shows a stale page.

new: Subtitle clean-up driven by Bazarr, with rules for PGS (picture) subtitles.
Fallback for films that never get forced subtitles.
Two ways to manage subtitles: Bazarr, or PMM's own built-in search and download with scoring, timing checks, retries, upgrades and quota handling.
Films without dialogue are recognised and don't need subtitles.
Optional subtitle position strip: SRT subtitles can be kept at the bottom of the screen (styled ASS subtitles keep their placement and effects).
Sign in with Authentik (OpenID Connect), including automatic sign-in.
Library views with switchable layouts (list, grid, item page styles) and artwork from Plex.
Libraries: choose the folders to index (or import them from Plex); everything is analysed continuously as a dry run on your workers, with nothing changed until you apply.
A new Overview home page with activity and workers, per-library tabs, readable page addresses and breadcrumbs.
"This server" setting: the main app can help process files, off by default so a NAS stays light.
Auto-apply: opt-in automatic applying of chosen change types (off by default).
MP4 and AVI files are planned for conversion to MKV (a remux, no re-encode) instead of being skipped.
Plex-aware pausing: a worker pauses only when Plex is busy on its machine or playing the file it's working on, and a rewritten file is never swapped in during playback.
Release feed and version scheme: four-part versions, with Develop and Release channels.
fixed: Foreign films keep their original-language audio instead of the dub.
Made-up languages (such as Klingon or Elvish) never lead to "English only, remove all subtitles".
Workers stop gracefully: the running file is handed back and cleaned up, and the worker service starts and logs correctly.
Free space is shown correctly for a scratch folder that doesn't exist yet.
changed: The Settings page has been redesigned.
The Review page is retired; its work now lives in the library tabs.
The Docker image is published under version tags (`0.2.0.0`, `0.2`, `latest`); preview builds are tagged `develop`.
